items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the state education department to enter into interstate reciprocity agreements and/or regional compacts for post-secondary distance education programs and to charge a fee to participating in-state institutions and non-participating out-of-state institutions that offer distance education; and to amend the state finance law, in relation to establishing an interstate reciprocity post-secondary distance education account
items.lawCode: Add §§210-c & 212, Ed L; add §97-llll, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5607

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
authorizing the state education department to enter into interstate
reciprocity agreements and/or regional compacts for post-secondary
distance education programs and to charge a fee to participating
in-state institutions and non-participating out-of-state institutions
that offer distance education; and to amend the state finance law, in
relation to establishing an interstate reciprocity post-secondary
distance education account

Purpose of the Bill:  The purpose of the "Interstate Reciprocity
Agreement for Post-Secondary Distance Education Programs" is to
authorize the State Education Department ("the Department") to enter
into interstate reciprocity agreements and/or regional compacts for
postsecondary distance education courses and programs and to authorize
the Department to charge a fee to participating in-state and
non-participating out-of-state institutions that offer distance
education.

Summary of the Provisions of the Bill:

Section 1 of the bill refers to the title of the bill as the
"Interstate Reciprocity Agreement for Post-Secondary Distance
Education Programs."

Section 2 sets forth the legislative intent.

Section 3 adds a new section 210-c to the Education Law to establish
the terms of the Interstate Reciprocity Agreement for Post-Secondary
Distance Education Programs.

Article I of this section sets forth the purpose, findings and policy
behind the Interstate Reciprocity Agreement.

Article II of this section defines, for purposes of this bill, the
following terms: "accredited "approve" or "approval", "complaint",
"council", "C-RAC guidelines", "distance education", "home state",
"institution", "legal domicile", "member state", "physical presence",
"portal agency", "regional compact" and "state authorization
reciprocity agreements" or "SARA".

Article III authorizes the Commissioner, on behalf of New York State,
to enter into the State Authorization Reciprocity Agreement ("SARA")
and/or any regional compacts on behalf of New York State with one more
other states to provide for the reciprocity of post-secondary distance
education programs and to carry out all activities necessary to carry
out such function. It also establishes the duties and responsibilities
of the Department under SARA.

Article IV of this section sets forth the eligibility requirements for
institutions seeking admission to SARA.

Article V of this section preserves the separate and distinct approval
process of other educational programs not approved under SARA.

Article VI of this section defines the terms for withdrawal from SARA.


Section 4 adds a new State Finance Law § 97-1111 to establish a
separate revenue account to be held in the joint custody of the State
Comptroller and the Commissioner of Taxation and Finance to receive
any appropriation or fees established necessary for services and
expenses incurred by the education department in conducting
evaluations, processing complaints or other administrative functions
related to post-secondary distance education programs.

Section 5 amends Education Law § 212 by adding a new subdivision 7 to
permit the Department to establish and charge fees for services and
expenses incurred by the department in conducting evaluations,
processing complaints or performing other administrative functions
related to the review of post-secondary distance education conducted
by out-of-state institutions seeking approval to offer distance
education to students in New York State who do not participate in SARA
pursuant to Education Law § 210-c.

Section 6 establishes an immediate effective date and authorizes the
addition, amendment or promulgation of any regulation necessary to
implement this bill to be made and completed on or before such
effective date; and requires the Commissioner to notify the
legislative bill drafting commission upon the occurrence of the
State's execution of SARA and/or a regional compact for distance
education, so the Commission may maintain an accurate and timely
effective database of the official text of those laws in accordance
with the Public Officers Law and the Legislative Law.

Statement in Support of the Bill:  This bill provides the Department
with the necessary statutory authority to allow New York institutions
of higher education (IHEs) to participate in an interstate reciprocity
agreement for postsecondary distance education. This legislation would
provide a mechanism for New York IHEs to offer distance education
programs to residents of participating states.

Over the past several years, the widespread availability of digital
and internet connected technologies has created greater opportunities
for institutions of higher education IHEs to provide programs of study
to students through distance education. The opportunity to offer
programs of study through distance education has opened up a new
marketplace for IHEs who can potentially enroll students who
physically reside in places other than where an IHE is located,
including other states.

Additionally, maintaining competitive stature in the national
marketplace for distance education is of critical importance for New
York State's colleges and universities. The declining population,
particularly upstate, and decreases in the number of students
projected to graduate from high school over the next several years are
forcing IHEs to consider changes in their allocation of resources,
recruitment strategies, investment decisions, tuition policies and
financial aid as they attempt to maintain their enrollment and remain
competitive. One strategy for maintaining or increasing enrollment is
the development of new course offerings that may be delivered through
distance education to in-state and out-of-state residents. However,
the approval by the Board of Regents and the Department of a New York
State IHE to offer distance education degree programs in-state does
not extend its authority to offer online programs to students residing


in other states. Because authorization requirements vary from state to
state, new challenges have emerged for IHEs in terms of gaining the
requisite state approvals to offer distance education to students
across state lines.  For example, some states may require full and
detailed program approval and review processes for out-of-state IHEs
seeking to offer distance education to its residents. Other states may
additionally require monetary fees from out-of-state IHEs for program
proposal review. As is the case in New York State, other states
require no specific state approval if the IHE is not establishing a
physical presence within the state. Navigating these separate and
varied approval processes can be time consuming, cumbersome and costly
for New York State IHEs.

This legislation would address the challenges of interstate
authorization of distance education, by authorizing the Commissioner
to enter into SARA or any regional compact on behalf of the State with
one or more other states to provide for the reciprocity of
postsecondary distance education and to carry out all activities
necessary to carry out that function. Furthermore, the eligibility of
IHEs to participate in such reciprocal agreements is contingent upon
state membership. Therefore, this legislation is necessary to permit
the expansion of postsecondary distance education programs.

The bill further permits the Department to charge any necessary fees
for services and expenses incurred by the Department in conducting
evaluations, processing complaints or performing other administrative
functions related to the review of post-secondary distance education
conducted by out-of-state institutions seeking approval to offer
distance education to students in New York State who do not
participate in an interstate reciprocity agreement. This additional
revenue will allow the Department to obtain the staff necessary to
effectively evaluate, approve and oversee these distance education
programs. Without this additional staff, the Department will not be
able to perform these additional duties necessary to participate in
SARA.

Prior Legislative History: This is a new bill.

Effective Date:  This act would take effect immediately; provided that
the addition, amendment or promulgation of any regulation necessary to
implement this bill be made and completed on or before such effective
date.
